uncited: The method transforms arbitrary parallel projection rays into a format suitable for parallel hardware processing.
It operates on a dataset stored in a Cubic Frame Buffer (CFB) and produces a 2D projected image.
The viewing direction is arbitrary (parallel projection).
**Retrieve Projection Ray Plane (PRP):** Identify the set of projection rays belonging to the same scan line of the projected 2D frame buffer.
**Fetch Beams:** Retrieve the PRP from the CFB as $n$ beams parallel to a primary axis.
**De-skew (Shear):** Shift each beam left or right within the 2DSB to align all viewing rays vertically (parallel to a 2D axis).
**Transfer to RPT:** Transfer rays to the RPT.
**Process Rays:** Process rays in parallel through the RPT.
*   *Standard:* Each VCU combines two voxels in 7 time units.
*   *Neighborhood (Optional):* For algorithms requiring a 27-voxel neighborhood (central voxel + 26 neighbors), use multiple parallel 2DSBs.
*   **Strengths:** Supports real-time arbitrary parallel projection without image distortion; conflict-free access to beams and rays; pipeline-friendly.
*   **When to Use:** When real-time arbitrary parallel projection of high-resolution volumes is required and hardware resources are available.
It builds on the Cube-3 Hybrid Ray-Casting method [3143-cube-3-hybrid-ray-casting.md].
